records.text: Aircraft can trick their transponders, and the relevant flights to Provo do not appear normally on flight-radar records.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It's going to look to you like this tail number SU-BTU. is just flying around in circles in Cairo, I have been able to confirm that they are able to trick their transponders and they can leave the nation. So it is a fact. You're not going to be able to see some flight radar.

verification.notes: FAA material confirms ADS-B/GPS signals can be spoofed, fail, or broadcast erroneous data, and public flight trackers can therefore have gaps or incorrect tracks. No authoritative source reviewed confirms that SU-BTU or the alleged Provo flights used spoofing, failed to transpond, or were absent for that reason.

sources.title: Getting to Know Your ADS-B System
sources.relevance: FAA explains ADS-B transmitters and position sources can fail or broadcast incorrect information, while requiring normal transmission unless authorized otherwise.

records.text: On October 7, 2023, the Egyptian aircraft SU-BTU flew from Cairo to Paris shortly after the attacks began, then flew from Paris to St. Louis and stayed there for five days.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: October 7th, 2023, a day that will live in infamy, probably for the Palestinians. The Egyptian plane, S-U-B-T-U, which I describe as my purple plane, flew from Cairo at 8.50 a.m. shortly after the attacks began. ... So did somebody fly in and then take them out? I don't know. That's just a fact. October 7th, that's what they did. They flew from Cairo to Paris. ... And, okay, random fact: then it flew from Paris to St. Louis, Missouri, and stayed for five days.

verification.notes: Transcript context clearly describes a purported SU-BTU itinerary, but no authoritative passenger or historical flight record located in current public sources establishes the Cairo-Paris-St. Louis routing or five-day stay. Audited public-record limitation; verification was attempted.

records.text: On April 14, 2024, during Iran and Hezbollah's retaliation for Israel's bombing of the Iranian embassy in Damascus, the Egyptian aircraft SU-BTU flew from Cairo to Paris and stayed there for six days.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Similarly, on April 14th of 2024—I believe I wrote 25, but I think it's 24—there was Operation True Promise, okay? ... That's when Israel was being bombed by Iran and Hezbollah in retaliation because Israel had bombed the Iranian embassy in Damascus. ... Well, lo and behold, that same Egyptian plane took off, flew from Cairo, always to Paris, and it stayed there for six days.

verification.notes: No authoritative public historical flight record located establishes SU-BTU flying Cairo to Paris on April 14, 2024 or remaining there six days. Current flight-tracking pages do not expose sufficient historical detail. Audited public-record limitation; verification was attempted.

records.text: SUBTT came from Cairo through Paris to Omaha, Nebraska on July 20th, stayed in Nebraska for six days departing from Lincoln, Nebraska, and stayed in Wilmington for one night.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: No, it only stayed in Wilmington for one night. It stayed in Nebraska for the longest stretch yet, departing from Lincoln, Nebraska, in particular.

verification.notes: Owens corrected the prior-day error, and the corrected route matches primary ADS-B reconstruction: Cairo via Paris to the Omaha/Lincoln area on July 20, six days at Lincoln, then Wilmington on July 26 and Cairo on July 27.

sources.relevance: Primary ADS-B reconstruction corroborates the corrected Cairo–Paris–Nebraska route, six-day Lincoln stay, and later Wilmington leg.
